stem: An adult has recurrent spontaneous vertigo episodes lasting 20 minutes to 12 hours, documented fluctuating low- to mid-frequency sensorineural hearing loss in one ear, tinnitus, and aural fullness. Which disorder is most consistent with this pattern?
rationale: The AAO-HNSF clinical practice guideline defines definite Ménière disease by spontaneous vertigo attacks lasting 20 minutes to 12 hours together with documented low- to mid-frequency sensorineural hearing loss in the affected ear and fluctuating aural symptoms such as tinnitus or pressure/fullness. D is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the defining symptom pattern of definite Ménière disease.
source_organization: American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Foundation (AAO-HNSF)
source_version_date: Published 2020-04-08; remains listed on AAO-HNSF current guideline inventory in 2026
source_locator: Guideline fact sheet / disease definition — spontaneous vertigo attacks 20 minutes to 12 hours with low- to mid-frequency sensorineural hearing loss; fluctuating tinnitus/ear pressure symptoms
source_claim_supported: Definite Ménière disease is characterized by episodic spontaneous vertigo of defined duration, documented sensorineural hearing loss, and fluctuating aural symptoms in the affected ear.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — sensory/vestibular alterations and clinical manifestations

source_original.stem: A client reports recurrent episodes of vertigo, fluctuating hearing loss, tinnitus, and a sensation of ear fullness, and a family member assumes these are just unrelated random symptoms with no single connecting cause. The nurse should recognize this classic symptom cluster as consistent with:

options.A: Vestibular migraine, which can cause episodic vertigo but does not require the characteristic fluctuating hearing loss and aural fullness described here.
options.B: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, which usually causes brief position-triggered attacks without the same fluctuating auditory symptom pattern.
options.C: Vestibular neuritis, which more often causes a prolonged acute vertigo syndrome without recurrent fluctuating hearing loss and aural fullness.
options.D: Ménière's disease, which classically causes recurrent episodic vertigo with fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and aural fullness.

source_original.rationale: The classic symptom tetrad of Ménière's disease includes recurrent episodic vertigo, fluctuating sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, and a sensation of aural (ear) fullness, resulting from abnormal fluid buildup in the inner ear, warranting evaluation by an ENT specialist for diagnosis and management.
source_original.source_detail: AAO-HNSF Clinical Practice Guideline: Ménière’s Disease, diagnostic key action statement and defining symptom complex. Published 2020-04-08; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Added the guideline's defining vertigo duration and documented sensorineural-hearing-loss criteria, removed family-member cueing and explanatory distractors, and removed the unnecessary causal claim about inner-ear fluid buildup. Reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: AAO-HNSF clinical practice guideline; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: AAO-HNSF continues to list the 2020 Ménière guideline as current in its 2026 guideline inventory.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Vertigo duration, documented low/mid-frequency SNHL, and fluctuating aural symptoms are directly supported by the guideline definition.

distractor_audit.A: Vestibular migraine does not require this documented cochlear pattern.
distractor_audit.B: BPPV is brief and position triggered rather than the defined spontaneous auditory syndrome.
distractor_audit.C: Vestibular neuritis classically causes a prolonged acute vestibular syndrome and not this fluctuating cochlear pattern.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The added duration and audiometric hearing-loss criterion make D uniquely defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: Removed long explanatory answer options and family interpretation.
audit_findings.blueprint: Vestibular/sensory physiologic alterations fit Physiological Adaptation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked AAO-HNSF current guideline and fact sheet; D remains uniquely correct.
